findings.finding: The note explicitly prints lęgde (lēde), (ge)lęgd (-lēd). The selected uncontracted citation is directly printed, not reconstructed.
The source directly supplies the ðōht/þōht participial citation. The policy describes only the declared thorn-to-eth spelling change; it does not derive new morphology.
The existing citation note and the new dictionary note each repeat the same two-sentence modal caveat.
findings.requested_change: Print the conventional-citation/Unit-6 caveat once and retain the separate no-participle statement.

specific_conclusions: All 81 added reference spellings, including vowel quantities, pass; no learner-form replacement is requested.
Strong participles follow the correct class vowel and consonant series; lexical prefixes survive unchanged.
The full -ed dental participles are expressly permitted by the selected source subdivisions; they are not generated merely by deleting preterite -e.

Cook lexical pp.293/306 explicitly place genēalǣcan/nēalǣcan in §113, independently supporting the chosen -ced formations. BT Supp.378 confirms both cte and hte past alternatives; the glossary does not silently replace the selected course series.
Āgen is explicitly adjectival. Cunnan, unnan and witan receive only the participles their individual source paradigms print.
The modal citation caveats and bounded-source entries make course/reference limits explicit; absence from the checked paradigm is not called universal nonattestation.
Pret. 1 sg. is the correct generic diagnostic label here: Cook p.62 explicitly gives findan third-singular funde.
All six identified inflected participle records are excluded from base diagnostic selection. Their actual lookup forms must remain in the internal index.
Optional ge is retained only from specific source citation notation; it is not an open-ended prefix-generation rule.
All 372 revised verb paragraphs and all 81 new forms were actually read in the Markdown master. No export/PDF acceptance is claimed.
